meaning: Flaps on a hat that fold down to cover the ears
trick: EAR + FLAPS: flaps that hang over your ears.
examples: He wore an enormous Russian fur hat with earflaps pulled down.
In winter my grandfather wears a woolly cap with earflaps.

usage.pattern: a hat with earflaps / pull down the earflaps

meaning: Very serious and sincere in what you say or do
trick: EARNEST sounds like 'honest' - serious and sincere.
examples: The man who came to give the news was so earnest.
He made an earnest promise to work harder.

usage.pattern: be earnest / an earnest + noun / in earnest

meaning: In a serious and sincere way, really meaning it
trick: EARNEST + -LY: saying it with an honest, serious face.
examples: "Yes, please," the girl said earnestly, almost eagerly.
She earnestly hoped her brother would get the job.

meaning: The quality of being serious and sincere
trick: EARNEST + -NESS: the state of being earnest.
examples: His look was one of guileless yet ironclad earnestness.
The earnestness in her voice made me trust her.

usage.pattern: with earnestness / the earnestness of someone

meaning: The lower edges of a roof that stick out over the walls
trick: Birds nest under the EAVES - the 'eave'-ning shade of the roof.
examples: Icicles hung like crystals from the eaves of houses.
Pigeons built a nest under the eaves of our house.

usage.pattern: under the eaves / from the eaves of something

meaning: Did better than or went beyond (a record or achievement); also made to look less important
trick: In an ECLIPSE the moon covers the sun - a new record covers the old one.
examples: Six weeks later, his record was eclipsed by another runner.
Her sales this year eclipsed last year's total.

usage.pattern: something is eclipsed by something / eclipse someone/something

meaning: Going beyond or surpassing (a number or record); also making something look less important
hindi: पार करते हुए, पीछे छोड़ते हुए
trick: ECLIPSING: covering the old mark, like the moon covering the sun.
examples: After eclipsing 3,200 pull-ups, I worked out the math.
The movie is eclipsing every box-office record this year.

meaning: Feelings of very great happiness or excitement
trick: ECSTASIES - 'ex-stasis': so happy you jump out of your place.
examples: The pigs were in ecstasies over Napoleon's cunning.
The children were in ecstasies over the new puppy.

meaning: A feeling of very great happiness
trick: ECSTASY - so happy you are 'ex-static', not standing still.
examples: In the ecstasy of that thought they leapt round and round in excitement.
Winning the match filled him with ecstasy.

usage.pattern: in ecstasy / the ecstasy of something

meaning: Extremely happy and excited
trick: ECSTATIC - so happy you feel electric (static)!
examples: Not long after, I received an ecstatic email from this student.
She was ecstatic when she passed the exam.

usage.pattern: be ecstatic about/at something / an ecstatic + noun

meaning: Swelling caused by too much fluid collecting in the body's tissues
trick: EDEMA - 'e-DEEMA': the leg puffs up like a balloon with water.
examples: Uncontrolled pneumonia can lead to pulmonary edema, which can be deadly.
The doctor said the swelling in her feet was edema.

meaning: A large, complex system of ideas or beliefs; also a large, impressive building
trick: EDIFICE - like 'edify' and 'office': a big built thing.
examples: On top of this false edifice of rationality was, of course, process.
The old palace is a grand edifice in the city centre.

meaning: In a strange way that feels a little frightening
hindi: अजीब तरह से, डरावने ढंग से
trick: EERIE + -LY: like hearing a creepy 'eee' sound.
examples: We end up feeling eerily similar to how we started: inadequate.
The street was eerily quiet at night.

meaning: Showing feelings in a very open, eager and lavish way
trick: EFFUSIVE - feelings 'effuse' (pour out) like a fountain.
examples: She filled all the spaces with effusive speech in a high, ringing voice.
He was effusive in his thanks after we helped him.

usage.pattern: be effusive in/about something / effusive + noun

meaning: A very clever, studious person (informal, often mocking)
trick: EGGHEAD - a big bald head like an egg, full of brains.
examples: He's an egghead now.
My cousin is an egghead who reads science books for fun.

usage.pattern: be an egghead / an egghead + noun

meaning: A large, shiny purple vegetable (British: aubergine)
trick: EGGPLANT - early ones were white and looked like eggs.
examples: He took a pinch of the pickled eggplant Mariam had made that summer.
My mother makes tasty curry with eggplant.

meaning: To get or make something with great difficulty, a little at a time (used with 'out')
hindi: मुश्किल से निकालना, खींचतान कर चलाना
trick: EKE - 'eek!': the last tiny squeak you squeeze out.
examples: She had to eke out the last few words in a tiny squeak.
They eke out a living by selling vegetables.

meaning: A medical test that records the heart's electrical activity (also ECG)
trick: EKG = ElectroKardioGram (German 'K') - the heart's zigzag line.
examples: It looked like an arrhythmic EKG.
The doctor ordered an EKG to check his heart.

meaning: Very detailed, long and carefully planned or worked out
trick: ELABORATE - lots of LABOUR went into it.
examples: The only things that caught my attention were some elaborate tirades.
They made an elaborate plan for the wedding.

meaning: Developed or explained something in more detail
trick: ELABORATED - put more LABOUR into an idea.
examples: These three had elaborated old Major's teachings into a complete system of thought.
The teacher elaborated on the topic after class.

usage.pattern: elaborated something into something / elaborated on something

meaning: Very happy and excited
trick: ELATED - 'elevated' mood, flying high.
examples: I thought I'd be elated, but I wasn't.
She was elated when she got the job offer.

meaning: To injure or kill someone with an electric shock
hindi: बिजली का झटका देना, करंट से मारना
trick: ELECTRO + exeCUTE: execute with electricity.
examples: I heard they electrocute prisoners there.
Don't touch that wire - it could electrocute you.

meaning: Injured or killed by an electric shock
hindi: बिजली का झटका लगा, करंट से मरा
trick: ELECTRO + exeCUTED.
examples: There were rumours of prisoners being electrocuted in the prison.
The worker was nearly electrocuted while fixing the fan.

meaning: A mineral such as salt or potassium in body fluids that carries an electric charge
trick: ELECTRO + LYTE: 'light' salts that carry electricity in your body.
examples: I didn't even consider my electrolyte or potassium levels.
Drink an electrolyte solution after long exercise.

meaning: Graceful and attractive in a simple, well-designed way
trick: ELEGANT - an ELEGANT ELEPHANT? No - think of a graceful swan.
examples: First come the walls, then the elegant but strong roof.
She wore an elegant black dress to the party.

meaning: Height above sea level; also the act of raising someone or something
trick: ELEVATION - an ELEVATOR takes you up to a higher elevation.
examples: The battle played out along a ridgeline above 9,000 feet in elevation.
The village is at an elevation of 2,000 metres.

usage.pattern: at an elevation of + number / in elevation

meaning: To get information or a reaction from someone
trick: ELICIT - 'E-LICK-it': lick it out of someone. (Not 'illicit' = illegal.)
examples: The tactics helped gain trust and elicit the verbalization of needs.
The teacher's question failed to elicit an answer.

meaning: Shaped like an oval; (as in a gym cross-trainer whose pedals move in an oval path)
trick: ELLIPTICAL - from ELLIPSE, a stretched circle.
examples: There was an elliptical trainer in the brand-new gym.
I use the elliptical machine for twenty minutes every morning.

meaning: Tall trees with broad leaves and rough bark
trick: ELMS - think 'helms': tall trees standing like guards.
examples: The pigeons cooed it in the elms.
Tall elms lined both sides of the old road.

usage.pattern: in the elms / a row of elms

meaning: To run away secretly to get married
trick: ELOPE - 'Let's E-LOPE (gallop) away and marry!'
examples: She'd tried to elope with a young man she'd fallen in love with.
The couple decided to elope because their parents disagreed.

usage.pattern: elope with someone / elope to somewhere

meaning: The skill of speaking or writing in a powerful, persuasive way
trick: ELOQUENCE - 'e-LOQU' = speak out (as in loquacious).
examples: In a moment Snowball's eloquence had carried them away.
The leader's eloquence moved the whole crowd.

usage.pattern: the eloquence of someone / speak with eloquence

meaning: To escape from or avoid someone or something, often cleverly; also to be hard to achieve or remember
trick: ELUDE - E + LUDE (Latin 'play'): play your way out.
examples: He seemed to think he'd somehow elude capture.
The thief managed to elude the police for weeks.

meaning: Difficult to find, catch, understand or achieve
hindi: मायावी, पकड़ में न आने वाला
trick: ELUSIVE - it always ELUDES you.
examples: I'd always been intrigued by it due to the elusive nature of the group.
Happiness can seem elusive when you chase it.

meaning: Extremely thin and weak because of illness or lack of food
trick: EMACIATED - 'e-MEAT-ciated': no meat left on the bones.
examples: By this time, he was emaciated and starved from the smallpox.
The rescued dog was emaciated and weak.

meaning: Extra details added to a story to make it more interesting, often not true; also decorations
trick: EMBELLISHMENTS - 'belle' = beautiful: making a story prettier.
examples: We fill in a couple of the plot holes with our own embellishments.
His fishing story had a lot of embellishments.

usage.pattern: with embellishments / add embellishments to something

meaning: A design or object that represents a group, idea or country
trick: EMBLEM - an EMBroidered badge on a blazer.
examples: The emblem tells the world we are not to be messed with.
The lion is the emblem of our school.

meaning: A person or thing that perfectly shows an idea or quality
trick: EMBODIMENT - an idea given a BODY.
examples: She was the walking, breathing embodiment of their shame.
My grandmother is the embodiment of kindness.

meaning: Made someone feel braver or more confident
trick: EMBOLDENED - made BOLD.
examples: Then, as if emboldened, the other women pushed past Fariba.
Emboldened by his success, he asked for a raise.

usage.pattern: be emboldened by something / embolden someone

meaning: Decorated with patterns sewn on with thread
trick: EMBROIDERED - 'broidered' sounds like 'braided' thread.
examples: The shawl's edges were embroidered with gold thread.
She wore a white kurta embroidered with blue flowers.

meaning: Famous and respected, especially in a particular field
trick: EMINENT - stands out like a mountain peak. (Not 'imminent' = about to happen.)
examples: Half a dozen of the more eminent pigs sat round the long table.
An eminent doctor spoke at the conference.

meaning: A person who can feel and understand other people's emotions very strongly
trick: EMPATH - from EMPATHy: feels what you feel.
examples: She believed she had become a healer and an empath.
As an empath, she always knows when her friends are sad.

meaning: To use a method, skill or tool; also to give someone a paid job
trick: EMPLOY - you employ workers AND employ tools: both get put to use.
examples: I had no idea where to employ backstops.
We must employ a new method to solve this problem.

usage.pattern: employ something / employ someone as something

meaning: A person or company that pays people to work for them
trick: EMPLOYER - the one who EMPLOYS; employee is the one employed.
examples: I have fixed up with my employer for two days' leave.
My employer gave me a bonus this year.

usage.pattern: someone's employer / work for an employer

meaning: To put something into action or act it out; also to make a law official
hindi: लागू करना, अमल में लाना; कानून बनाना
trick: EN-ACT: put it into ACTion.
examples: How we are is the easiest thing to enact and the most effective.
The government will enact a new law next month.

meaning: A hard, shiny, coloured coating on metal or pottery; also the hard surface of teeth
trick: ENAMEL - think 'meena-kari': shiny colour on silver.
examples: Tariq bought silver earrings with an enamel butterfly on each.
Brushing too hard can damage your tooth enamel.

meaning: Charmed or delighted greatly; also put under a magic spell
trick: ENCHANTED - as if a magic CHANT was sung.
examples: The tiniest changes in the baby enchanted her.
The children were enchanted by the puppet show.

usage.pattern: something enchants someone / be enchanted by something

meaning: Very charming and delightful
trick: ENCHANTING - like a magic CHANT pulling you in.
examples: He liked the enchanting sounds the Arabic words made.
The hill station has an enchanting view of the valley.

meaning: A feeling of great delight, as if under a spell; also magic
trick: ENCHANTMENT - the state of being under a CHANT.
examples: Whenever Jalil talked like this, Mariam would listen with enchantment.
The old town has a special enchantment at night.

usage.pattern: with enchantment / the enchantment of something

meaning: Words or actions that express love or affection
trick: ENDEARMENTS - words that make you DEAR to someone.
examples: Jalil came every Thursday, all smiles and gifts and endearments.
Grandma always greets us with hugs and endearments.

meaning: To try very hard to do something (US spelling; British 'endeavour'); also an attempt or effort
trick: ENDEAVOR - 'END-eavor': try till the END.
examples: I will always endeavor to uphold the honor of the Rangers.
We endeavor to reply to every email within a day.

meaning: Relating to the glands that make hormones and release them into the blood
trick: ENDO (inside) + CRINE (secrete): glands secreting inside the body.
examples: His office tested my endocrine system.
The thyroid is part of the endocrine system.

meaning: Chemicals made in the brain that reduce pain and make you feel good
trick: ENDORPHINS - ENDO + mORPHINE: the body's own painkiller.
examples: Some scientists think it's the result of endorphins flooding your nervous system.
A morning run releases endorphins and lifts my mood.

meaning: To suffer something painful patiently; also to last a long time
trick: ENDURE - hold on till the END.
examples: Despite the cruelties of their world, the heroines do endure.
She had to endure a lot of pain after the surgery.

meaning: Suffered something painful or difficult patiently
trick: ENDURED - held on until the END.
examples: This is my reward for everything I've endured.
They endured a long, cold winter without heating.

meaning: A person or thing that is against or harms someone or something
trick: ENEMY - 'an-NOT-my' friend.
examples: Certainty is the enemy of growth.
Laziness is the biggest enemy of success.

usage.pattern: the enemy of something / someone's enemy

meaning: Marked deeply with lines or cuts; also with words cut into a hard surface
trick: ENGRAVED - like letters cut into a GRAVE stone.
examples: Her arms and back were engraved with marks of pain.
His name was engraved on the silver trophy.

usage.pattern: be engraved with something / engraved on something

meaning: To surround and cover something completely
trick: ENGULF - a GULF of water swallows everything.
examples: She watched the shadows engulf the neighboring house-fronts.
Flames began to engulf the old building.

meaning: Things or people that are mysterious and hard to understand
trick: ENIGMAS - the ENIGMA machine made secret codes nobody could read.
examples: They are existential riddles wrapped in enigmas.
Some of life's enigmas will never be solved.

usage.pattern: be an enigma / enigmas of something

meaning: (Of soldiers) belonging to the ranks below officers; also joined the armed forces
trick: ENLISTED - your name is on the LIST of ordinary soldiers.
examples: When you're an enlisted guy and an Admiral wants a word, you get nervous.
My uncle enlisted in the army at eighteen.

usage.pattern: an enlisted + noun / enlisted in something

meaning: The great size or seriousness of something, especially something important or bad
trick: ENORMITY - ENORMous importance.
examples: Both of them were speechless before the enormity of what had just happened.
He slowly realised the enormity of his mistake.

meaning: Extremely large
trick: ENORMOUS - 'E-NORMOUS': out of the NORM in size.
examples: It showed an enormous face, more than a metre wide.
They live in an enormous house near the beach.

meaning: To a very great degree
trick: ENORMOUS + -LY.
examples: England could feed an enormously greater number of animals.
The book was enormously popular with children.

meaning: Settled in a safe, comfortable place
hindi: आराम से जमा हुआ, बैठा हुआ
trick: ENSCONCED - snug in a 'sconce' (a cosy nook).
examples: Major was already ensconced on his bed of straw.
The cat was ensconced on the warm sofa.

meaning: Caught or trapped in something difficult to escape
trick: ENSNARED - caught in a SNARE (trap).
examples: When you become ensnared in activities that don't better you, move on!
The bird was ensnared in a fishing net.

meaning: To happen after something, often as a result of it
trick: ENSUE - sounds like 'and SUE': a fight, and then a lawsuit follows.
examples: Panic attacks ensue; tears are shed.
When the lights went out, chaos ensued.

meaning: A difficult or complicated situation you are involved in
trick: ENTANGLEMENT - TANGLED up like knotted wires.
examples: Some business entanglement might prevent Jalil from coming on Thursday.
He avoided any legal entanglement with the company.

meaning: To persuade someone to do something by offering something attractive
trick: ENTICE - offer 'NICE' things to tempt someone.
examples: I'd written the letter so as to entice his mistress to his room.
The shop uses big discounts to entice customers.

usage.pattern: entice someone to do something / entice someone into something

meaning: Persuaded someone by offering something attractive
trick: ENTICED - lured with something NICE.
examples: I enticed her to come along by promising a vacation.
The smell of fresh bread enticed us into the bakery.

usage.pattern: enticed someone to do something / into something

meaning: Attractive and tempting
trick: ENTICING - something so NICE you can't resist.
examples: This feels sexy and enticing and may feel good for a while.
The cake in the window looked very enticing.

meaning: Believing you deserve special treatment without earning it; also having a right to something
trick: ENTITLED - acts like they hold a TITLE (lord) and deserve everything.
examples: Entitled people exude a delusional degree of self-confidence.
She's entitled to her own opinion.

usage.pattern: entitled + people / be entitled to something / to do something

meaning: The inner organs of an animal or person, especially the intestines
trick: ENTRAILS - the TRAIL of tubes inside a body.
examples: In one downward stroke, she removed the gills and the entrails of the fish.
The cook cleaned the fish and threw away the entrails.

meaning: So beautiful or interesting that you can't stop watching
trick: ENTRANCING - puts you in a TRANCE.
examples: What was it about a season's first snowfall that was so entrancing?
The dancer's movements were entrancing.

meaning: A person who starts and runs their own business, taking financial risks
trick: ENTREPRENEUR - 'enter-preneur': ENTERs business on their own.
examples: The idea of being an entrepreneur had always appealed to me.
My friend left his job to become an entrepreneur.

meaning: Wanted something that someone else has; felt jealous of
trick: ENVIED - 'ENVY-d': green with envy.
examples: Your friend Rumi would have envied my production.
Everyone envied her new car.

meaning: Extremely long periods of time
trick: EONS - 'EONS' sounds like 'aeons' = ages and ages.
examples: Seconds on that clock now feel like Paleolithic eons.
It's been eons since I last saw my school friends.

meaning: The central point of an activity; also the point on the ground above an earthquake's origin
hindi: केंद्र, मुख्य स्थान; भूकंप का केंद्र
trick: EPI (upon) + CENTER: the very centre of the action.
examples: Harvard had been the world epicenter of negotiating theory.
Mumbai is the epicenter of India's film industry.

meaning: To be a perfect example of something
hindi: का आदर्श उदाहरण होना, प्रतीक होना
trick: EPITOMIZE - 'epi-TOME': the whole book in one example.
examples: The case came to epitomize everything not to do in a crisis.
Her hard work epitomizes the spirit of our team.

meaning: A state of balance or calm
trick: EQUI (equal) + LIBRA (scales): equal on both sides.
examples: Psychological pain shows that something is out of equilibrium.
Yoga helps me keep my emotional equilibrium.

meaning: Going in the wrong direction or out of place; also behaving badly
trick: ERRANT - from ERR: something that has gone wrong.
examples: You are now one errant shoelace-trip away from disaster.
An errant ball broke the neighbour's window.

meaning: Not steady or regular; changing without warning
trick: ERRATIC - from ERR: wandering all over the place.
examples: They saw the Taliban like an erratic cousin prone to unpredictable acts.
His erratic driving scared all of us.

meaning: Started suddenly and strongly; also (of a volcano) burst out
trick: ERUPTED - like a volcano ERUPTING.
examples: Within six months, Beatlemania had erupted.
Laughter erupted when the teacher slipped.

meaning: Becoming bigger, worse or more serious
trick: ESCALATING - going up like an ESCALATOR.
examples: Not only was the bickering still going on, it was escalating.
Escalating prices are hurting families.

meaning: A long, steep slope or cliff at the edge of a high area
trick: ESCARPMENT - a SCARP (steep face) like a scar on the hill.
examples: The road winds up a parched rock escarpment for ten miles.
We hiked to the top of the escarpment for the view.

meaning: A person who goes with someone to protect or guide them
trick: ESCORT - 'ESCape-proof CORT': someone who walks beside you for safety.
examples: No women outside the house without a male escort.
The minister arrived with a police escort.

meaning: Went with someone to guide or protect them
trick: ESCORT = a guard who goes along with you.
examples: Afsoon escorted her back to the room upstairs.
The guard escorted the old man across the road.

meaning: Understood by only a few people with special knowledge
trick: ESOTERIC - 'eso' = inside: only for insiders.
examples: I taught myself web design, marketing and other esoteric topics.
His hobby is collecting esoteric old maps.

meaning: To openly support a belief or cause; also (old) to marry
trick: ESPOUSE - like a SPOUSE, you 'marry' an idea and stand by it.
examples: Onoda tried to use his fame to espouse the values of Old Japan.
Many young people espouse the idea of saving water.

usage.pattern: espouse a cause / a belief / values

meaning: In the most basic or important way; when you come down to it
trick: ESSENTIALLY = in ESSENCE.
examples: Both he and his commander knew it was essentially a suicide mission.
The two phones are essentially the same.

meaning: No longer living with or friendly with a family member or partner
trick: ESTRANGED - became a STRANGER to your own family.
examples: He had murdered his estranged wife and the pilot.
She called her estranged brother after ten years.

usage.pattern: estranged + wife/husband/family / be estranged from someone

meaning: Fixed firmly in the mind; also cut or carved into a surface
trick: ETCHED - like letters scratched into stone, they never fade.
examples: His movements were permanently etched in my brain like a cave painting.
Her name was etched on the silver cup.

usage.pattern: be etched in someone's memory / etched with something

meaning: Lasting forever or seeming to have no end
trick: ETERNAL - ETERNITY never ends.
examples: I was on an eternal march beneath a black sky full of stars.
The queue at the bank felt eternal.

meaning: A set of beliefs about how to behave, especially an attitude to hard work
trick: ETHIC - ETHICS = right and wrong; work ethic = how seriously you work.
examples: My work ethic is the most important factor in all my success.
Her strong work ethic got her promoted.

usage.pattern: a/the + work ethic / the ethic of something

meaning: Belonging to a group of people with a shared race, culture or language
trick: ETHNIC - ETHNIC food comes from a particular people's culture.
examples: Tariq and his parents were ethnic Pashtuns but spoke Farsi around Laila.
The city has many ethnic restaurants.

meaning: The typical spirit, values and attitudes of a group
trick: ETHOS - the 'ethics' that a group lives by.
examples: He was still living the SEAL ethos every day.
The school's ethos is kindness and hard work.

usage.pattern: the ethos of something / live the ethos

meaning: The accepted rules of polite behaviour
trick: ETIQUETTE - like a 'ticket' you need to enter polite society.
examples: Then there was my etiquette, which needed work too.
Table etiquette says you shouldn't talk with food in your mouth.

meaning: A strong feeling of great happiness and excitement
trick: EUPHORIA - 'eu' = good + 'phoria' = feeling: feeling very good.
examples: She had another of those little sparks of euphoria.
There was euphoria in the streets after the win.

usage.pattern: a feeling/sense of euphoria / in euphoria

meaning: Feeling or causing intense happiness and excitement
trick: EUPHORIC - in a state of EUPHORIA.
examples: The fear was becoming euphoric and blinding.
The fans were euphoric after the final goal.

meaning: Disappeared gradually; also turned from liquid into vapour
trick: EVAPORATED - like water in the sun, the feeling dried up.
examples: The earlier pleasure over his approval of her cooking had evaporated.
The puddle evaporated in the afternoon heat.

meaning: Becoming smaller and smaller all the time
trick: EVER + DWINDLING - always getting less, like a candle burning down.
examples: We save our ever-dwindling energy for what truly matters: family and friends.
Our ever-dwindling savings worried us.

meaning: Forced to leave a home or building by law
trick: EVICTED - 'e' = out + 'vict' (like VICTory): the landlord wins and you're out.
examples: You aren't getting evicted because of other people.
The family was evicted for not paying rent.

usage.pattern: be/get evicted from somewhere / evict someone

meaning: Morally very bad and cruel; also great harm
trick: EVIL is LIVE spelled backwards.
examples: Evil people never believe that they are evil.
The villain had an evil laugh.

usage.pattern: be evil / an evil + noun / good and evil

meaning: To destroy or weaken completely; also to remove the insides of
trick: EVISCERATE - 'e' = out + 'viscera' = guts: rip the guts out of something.
examples: It's up to you to find ways to eviscerate your excuses.
The critic eviscerated the new film in his review.

meaning: Made a problem or bad situation worse
trick: EXACERBATED - EXTRA ACID on a wound makes it worse.
examples: He could barely breathe, which exacerbated his problem.
The rain exacerbated the traffic jam.

usage.pattern: something exacerbated something / be exacerbated by something

meaning: To make something seem bigger, better or worse than it really is
trick: EXAGGERATE - double G, because you double everything.
examples: Yes, sometimes I exaggerate my own successes.
Don't exaggerate, it was only a small scratch.

meaning: Very annoyed and frustrated, especially after a long time
trick: EXASPERATED - so fed up you let out an EXASperated breath.
examples: She was more exhausted than exasperated.
The teacher was exasperated by the noisy class.

meaning: A feeling of great annoyance and frustration
trick: EXASPERATION - the feeling of being EXASPERATED.
examples: He looked at me with a mix of respect and funny exasperation.
She threw up her hands in exasperation.

meaning: Did something extremely well; was very good at something
trick: EXCELLED - became EXCELLENT.
examples: At my new university I excelled for the first time.
She excelled at maths in school.

meaning: The quality of being outstanding or extremely good
trick: EXCELLENCE - what EXCELLENT things have.
examples: The cost of missing so much excellence in this world felt huge to me.
The hospital is known for its excellence in care.

usage.pattern: excellence in something / a centre of excellence

meaning: Acts of doing or having too much of something, especially pleasures
trick: EXCESSES - EXCESS = more than needed; many such binges.
examples: As with most excesses in life, you have to drown in them to see they don't make you happy.
After the holiday excesses, he started a diet.

meaning: Said something suddenly and loudly from surprise or strong feeling
trick: EXCLAIMED - EXCLAMATION mark (!) at the end.
examples: "What's that?" he exclaimed.
"What a lovely surprise!" she exclaimed.

meaning: Extremely painful; also very embarrassing or boring
trick: EXCRUCIATING - 'cruci' = CROSS: pain like being on a cross.
examples: My left ear was throbbing in excruciating pain.
Waiting for the exam results was excruciating.

meaning: Gave a reason to explain or justify a fault; also allowed to leave
trick: EXCUSED - gave an EXCUSE.
examples: She was late every morning and excused herself by saying she had overslept.
He excused himself and left the table.

usage.pattern: excused oneself (by doing something) / be excused from something

meaning: Strong expressions of hatred or curses
trick: EXECRATION - sounds like 'EXECUTION': the crowd curses the condemned man.
examples: I hoped the crowd would greet me with howls of execration.
The traitor's name was met with execration.

meaning: To use power, influence or effort
trick: EXERT - put EXTRA effort out.
examples: She had no authority to exert over him.
Parents exert a lot of influence on their children.

meaning: Used power, influence or pressure on someone
trick: EXERTED - the past of EXERT: pushed with force.
examples: He kept talking about the influence the other robbers exerted on him.
The crowd exerted pressure on the gate.

meaning: Hard physical or mental effort
trick: EXERTION - what you do when you EXERT yourself.
examples: Slow, repetitive physical exertion puts me in a trancelike state.
He was red-faced from the exertion of climbing the stairs.

usage.pattern: physical exertion / the exertion of doing something

meaning: A state of being extremely tired
trick: EXHAUSTION - your energy's EXHAUST pipe is empty.
examples: His eyes were streaming with tears of exhaustion.
She fell asleep from exhaustion.

meaning: To show a quality or feeling; also to put on public display
trick: EXHIBIT - an EXHIBITION shows things to people.
examples: Often they grew up with parents who each exhibit one of these traits.
Some dogs exhibit fear during storms.

meaning: Shown at a public show or exhibition; also displayed a quality
trick: EXHIBITED - put on show at an EXHIBITION.
examples: The name under which he had been exhibited was Willingdon Beauty.
Her paintings were exhibited in Delhi.

usage.pattern: be exhibited at somewhere / exhibited something

meaning: Making you feel very happy and excited
trick: EXHILARATING - like a HILARIOUS ride: you scream with joy.
examples: The feeling was exhilarating.
The roller-coaster ride was exhilarating.

meaning: A feeling of great happiness and excitement
trick: EXHILARATION - the feeling from something EXHILARATING.
examples: Despite the exhilaration inside, she fell asleep.
He felt pure exhilaration at the top of the hill.

usage.pattern: a feeling/sense of exhilaration / with exhilaration

meaning: Relating to human existence and the meaning of life; also threatening survival
trick: EXISTENTIAL - about why we EXIST.
examples: Our crisis is no longer material; it's existential.
Turning forty gave him some existential worries.

meaning: A time of doubting the meaning or purpose of your life
trick: EXISTENTIAL CRISIS - 'Why do I EXIST?' panic.
examples: The prince returned to the palace and found himself in an existential crisis.
Losing his job sent him into an existential crisis.

meaning: Unusual and interesting because it comes from a distant place
trick: EXOTIC - 'exo' = outside: from outside your world.
examples: Teachers and students stared at me like I was some exotic species.
The zoo has many exotic birds.

meaning: In a way that shows you are waiting for something to happen
hindi: उम्मीद से, आशा भरी नज़रों से
trick: EXPECTANTLY - EXPECTING something any moment.
examples: She looked over expectantly.
The dog looked up expectantly at the food.

meaning: An organised journey for a purpose, such as exploring
trick: EXPEDITION - 'ex' + 'ped' (foot): going out on foot to explore.
examples: He signed up to join an expedition to the Amazon rain forest.
They went on an expedition to climb Everest.

usage.pattern: an expedition to somewhere / go on an expedition

meaning: Officially forced to leave a school or organisation
trick: EXPELLED - 'ex' = out + 'pel' = push: pushed out.
examples: Having been expelled from school, I was homeschooled for the rest of the year.
He was expelled for cheating in the exam.

meaning: Able to be explained or understood
trick: EXPLICABLE - can be EXPLAINED (opposite: inexplicable).
examples: The thief killed him for no explicable reason.
His anger was explicable once we heard the story.

usage.pattern: be explicable / an explicable + noun (often 'no explicable reason')

meaning: To argue or protest strongly with someone
trick: EXPOSTULATE - EXPOSE your complaint loudly.
examples: Raymond began to expostulate, and my lawyer, too, protested.
She started to expostulate about the unfair fine.

meaning: Explained or described something in detail
trick: EXPOUNDED - EXPLAINED with a POUND of detail.
examples: They held secret meetings and expounded the principles of Animalism.
The professor expounded his theory for an hour.

meaning: The act of forcing someone to leave a place or group
trick: EXPULSION - the noun of EXPEL.
examples: Despite the shock of Snowball's expulsion, the animals were dismayed.
The fight led to his expulsion from school.

meaning: Extremely beautiful, fine or delightful
trick: EXQUISITE - so EXcellent it's a QUIck SITE to remember.
examples: 'What if' is an exquisite reply to anyone who has ever doubted you.
She wore an exquisite silk sari.

meaning: Making a wrong action seem less serious or more excusable
trick: EXTENUATING - makes the blame 'TENUOUS' (thin).
examples: He pleaded guilty, but with extenuating circumstances.
Because of extenuating circumstances, she got extra time.

meaning: A reason that makes a wrong act seem less serious
trick: EXTENUATION - the excuse that EXTENUATES (thins) the blame.
examples: A sudden impulse might serve as extenuation for the crime.
He offered his illness in extenuation of his absence.

usage.pattern: in extenuation of something / serve as extenuation

meaning: A person whose job is killing insects, rats and other pests
trick: EXTERMINATOR - he TERMINATES the pests.
examples: It was my job to unlock the hospital kitchen for the exterminator.
We called an exterminator to get rid of the cockroaches.

meaning: Spending too much money or using too much of something
trick: EXTRAVAGANCE - EXTRA spending beyond what you need.
examples: He gave her enough money to live on, without extravagance.
Buying a new car every year is pure extravagance.

meaning: Spending or costing much more than is sensible
trick: EXTRAVAGANT - EXTRA + VAGANT (wandering): money wanders away.
examples: They no longer had to support five extravagant human beings.
They threw an extravagant wedding party.

meaning: Holding extreme political or religious views, often supporting violence
trick: EXTREMIST - goes to the EXTREME.
examples: Al Qaeda allied with existing extremist networks in Africa.
The police arrested members of an extremist group.

meaning: Frees someone or something from a difficult situation or place
trick: EXTRICATES - 'ex' = out of + 'tric' (like TRICKy) : out of a tricky spot.
examples: Travel extricates you from the values of your culture.
He carefully extricates the cat from the tree branches.

meaning: Full of energy, excitement and cheerfulness
trick: EXUBERANT - like an EXcited UBER driver singing all the way.
examples: This willing and even exuberant facing of death has ancient roots.
The exuberant children ran around the park.

meaning: To show a quality or feeling strongly; also to give off a smell or liquid
trick: EXUDE - 'ex' = out + 'ude' (like sweat): it oozes out of you.
examples: Entitled people exude a crazy degree of self-confidence.
Good leaders exude calm in a crisis.

meaning: Showing a quality or feeling strongly
trick: EXUDING - confidence oozing out of you.
examples: If he approaches exuding calm, the inmate will likely stay peaceful.
She walked in exuding confidence.

meaning: Very happy and proud because of a success
trick: EXULTANT - EXcited + reSULT: happy about the result.
examples: My lawyer was exultant.
The exultant team lifted the trophy.

meaning: A feeling of great happiness and triumph
trick: EXULTATION - the joy of a great RESULT.
examples: The thought flooded my mind with a wild, absurd exultation.
There were shouts of exultation when the results came.

usage.pattern: in exultation / a feeling of exultation

meaning: Looking hard at someone, often to judge or challenge them (informal)
trick: EYEBALLING - fixing your EYEBALLS on someone.
examples: Even with Psycho eyeballing me, I couldn't hide it.
The coach was eyeballing the new players.

meaning: Looking at someone or something carefully, often with interest (also spelled 'eyeing')
trick: EYING - using your EYES on something you want.
examples: The old fellows stood solemnly eying me.
The boy was eying the last piece of cake.
